column2: Mr. Mikimoto, you say?{r}{p}Ever since he arrived, he's been in the lounge almost the whole time.”
“He only went up to the second floor once, I'm sure...”
{n2} tilted her gaze slightly upward, searching her memory.
just long enough to drop off his luggage, so it can't have taken two minutes.{r}{p}How could he possibly kill Mr. Tanaka and cut up the body in that little time?”
{n2} was defending Mr. Mikimoto an awful lot.
Could it be she had a crush on him?
With that needless thought in my head, I said:
“If Mr. Mikimoto had actually arrived much earlier, cutting up Mr. Tanaka would be possible.”
I stared at him as I said it.
{n2} cut between our gazes and asked.
...So right after dinner he sneaked into Mr. Tanaka's room through the window and took his time cutting up the body?”
“You're forgetting that he phoned after dinner.{r}{p}Listen,
he called here from outside.{r}{p}Right at the time when, by your reasoning, he'd have been cutting up the body on the second floor.”
that.{r}{p}He must have used a cell phone.”
I told you they don't work around here.{p}And there are no houses or pay phones nearby.{r}{p}There wasn't time to cut up the body and make a round trip to town.”
I really shouldn't say careless things.
I stayed quiet for a while, but realized I couldn't leave it like this, so I got down from the sofa and put my hands on the floor.
Think a bit more before you speak, honestly.”
{n2} was talking as if I were a complete idiot.
“There wasn't time to cut up the body, but he could have killed Mr. Tanaka.”
a professional killer could kill someone in an instant, but...{@}
...{r}{p}Then when was the body cut up?”

he could attach a special device where he wants to cut, like the neck or shoulder.{r}{p}A device that tightens little by little as time passes and cuts through the body.{r}{p}If you make the blade from a shape-memory alloy, I think it's doable.”
I was fairly confident in this deduction.
But instead of being impressed, everyone looked utterly dumbfounded.
There was nothing like that anywhere.”
“Of course, he'd retrieve such devices once the cutting was done.”

There was no chance.{r}{p}Mr. Mikimoto only went up once, didn't he?{r}{p}He didn't even enter the room when the body was found, and setting up a device like that, besides the killing, would take as long as the cutting, wouldn't it?”
I really shouldn't say careless things.
I stayed quiet for a while, but realized I couldn't leave it like this, so I got down from the sofa and put my hands on the floor.
“Mr. Mikimoto, I'm sorry!{r}{p}I called you the culprit without any real basis, I don't know how to apologize...”
Maybe I was overdoing it a little.
Mr. Mikimoto, on the contrary, seemed flustered.
“No, no, it's all right.{r}{p}In a situation like this, it's natural to suspect each other.{r}{p}People you don't know well always look more suspicious.{r}{p}I'm not bothered.”
He surely was a bit bothered, but I was relieved that he said so.
Well, since we weren't even friends to begin with, I suppose being called the culprit didn't shock him much.
I reflected that from now on I'd have to act more carefully.
That's right, everyone here is the kind of person who couldn't hurt a fly.
What was I thinking, suspecting people like this?
“It's true he couldn't have killed Mr. Tanaka, but he could have killed Mr. Suzuki, couldn't he?”
I don't know the real name.{r}{p}In America, I hear they call unidentified bodies 'John Doe' or something.”
“I mean, I don't know whose body that chopped-up corpse is, but I'm saying it isn't Mr. Tanaka.”
“I told you, I don't know whose it is.{r}{p}Listen,
neither Mr. Mikimoto nor anyone else could have killed and cut up Mr. Tanaka.{r}{p}But there's a chopped-up body there.{r}{p}That means that body isn't Mr. Tanaka.{r}{p}It's that simple.”
When I said it, an uncomfortable silence took over for a while.
what are you saying?{r}{p}The culprit means whoever killed Mr. Tanaka, right?{r}{p}What do you mean the culprit is Mr. Tanaka?”
Mr. Kayama said, and Toshio burst out laughing.
If there's a way to chop yourself up, I'd like to be taught it.”
“...I'm not saying he killed himself.{r}{p}I never said I know who killed Mr. Tanaka.{r}{p}Listen,
we were all mistaken.{r}{p}The body upstairs isn't the man who checked in under the name Tanaka.”
...I started to say it, but hesitated.
This cheerful ski-loving man drinking coffee next to me...
I just couldn't believe he'd kill a person and cut them up.
But {n4} didn't have time to cut up a body.”
“Calling someone the culprit without enough evidence is the worst.”
I really shouldn't say careless things.
I decided to think it over carefully once more.
I didn't want to say anything rash again, so that's what I told {n2}, but I had just remembered something serious.
I remembered that when the sound of the window breaking came, there was exactly one person who wasn't in the lounge.
“Earlier, when I asked if the culprit was among the people we know, you said yes.”
“I just wanted to try saying something random.”
I said, laughing and puffing out my chest.
Here I was listening seriously and you...{r}{p}You're the worst!”
This time I'll say it properly.{r}{p}The culprit is...”
what are you saying?{r}{p}Mr. Tanaka is dead.”
You're right.{r}{p}What I meant to say was this: the culprit is Mr. Mikimoto.”
But I didn't name him right away; first I began by addressing everyone.
Everyone cried out in astonishment at once.
{n2} said, looking at me with worry.
“It was suicide.{r}{p}Midori failed to kill Mr. Mikimoto and gave up, thinking she'd be caught when he woke up.”
what are you saying?{r}{p}Midori had no chance to kill Mr. Tanaka or attack Mr. Mikimoto!{r}{p}How could she have done that?”
that I'll work out from here...”
